summary.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 10% to INR2,852 crore; Crop Care fell 16.2% on delayed monsoon, while management still targets double-digit FY27 PBT growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10% YoY to INR2,852 crore despite a delayed monsoon and geopolitical-driven inflation. Animal Nutrition (revenue +12.6%, reported segment result +29%) and Oil Palm (revenue +28.9%, segment result +14.4%) carried the quarter. Crop Care revenue fell 16.2% on a dry June and slower kharif sowing, and Dairy margins were squeezed by milk procurement costs and packaging inflation. Astec reached EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago. Management reiterated FY27 double-digit consolidated PBT growth (versus earlier mid-teens guidance) but deferred a firmer view on Crop Care until end-September.

financial_highlights.change: Cattle feed volume +15%; total segment volume +7%
Segment result +14.4%; EBIT margin ~17% vs 19% a year ago (per analyst)
vs EBITDA loss of INR11 crore in Q1 FY26
Value-added share of sales 49% vs 42% a year ago

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue +12.6% on robust demand and better realisations; cattle feed volume +15% and overall segment volume +7%. Poultry volumes deliberately reduced in unprofitable geographies. Cattle feed is about 55-56% of the segment; fish feed about 7%.

segments.name: Oil Palm
segments.commentary: Revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations and volume; FFB volumes broadly flat versus a strong early-monsoon base. Segment result +14.4%, with margin down on a pricing-formula effect that management calls one-off.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Revenue -16.2% as a dry June and slow kharif sowing hit cotton herbicide volumes, with margin contraction. Ashitaka and Takai together contribute about 18-20% of Q1 sales; Ghassnash soybean herbicide launched.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago; revenue moderately lower on product mix. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of more than 20%, with an 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO dissilience around 50-52%.

segments.name: Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.4% and volume +8%, but profitability hit by elevated milk procurement prices and packaging inflation. Route-to-market reconstitution (about 18-20 months) under new CEO Gaurav is starting.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable as live bird trading is planned to fall 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years. Branded B2C (Yummiez, Real Good) volume +28% and about 32% of the Foods business; profitability hit by input costs.

segments.name: Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet)
segments.commentary: Returned to growth, with double-digit growth in volume, revenue and PBT.

qa_highlights.question: What FFB volume growth and EBITDA trajectory can Oil Palm deliver over 3-5 years, and what capex and returns are involved in value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kataria guided FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over 4-5 years, targeting double digit; specialty fats refinery to start in September, with a 16-18% IRR hurdle and about 200 bps EBITDA uplift at scale. He did not give an explicit EBITDA number.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Care recover in H2, and is the consolidated mid-teens PBT growth still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was hit by a 40% June deficit; July is better than last year's base, and it will decide on the recovery by end-September. Consolidated growth now targeted at double digit, with the exact level to be given by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Astec: revenue outlook and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Arijit Mukherjee said FY27 revenue growth is now expected at more than 20%, with the 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO margins intact and enterprise margin normalising as prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Will the palm oil shift need extra capex, and what is the Foods/Dairy pricing picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex stays within the INR300-350 crore envelope already guided. Dairy volume grew 8% but packaging and milk costs hit margin; Foods B2C is in a 3-4 year investment phase, with live bird trading being wound down.

qa_highlights.question: How much maize inflation has Animal Nutrition passed through, and what is EBIT per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60-70% of commodity cost increases passed on; EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150, with Q1 EBITDA per tonne in that range or slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Oil Palm segment margin fall from 19% to 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to a one-off pricing-formula change in the quarter and flat FFB, offset by better OER; expects margins to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Crop Care lagging peers, and what are margins on the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is segment-mix and macro driven (cotton herbicide concentration), not share loss; new products carry lower margin than Hitweed but healthy, with total Crop Care EBIT margin seen at about 26-27%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated PBT growth: management still targets double-digit growth, narrowed from the earlier mid-teens guidance; exact position in the range to be given by end-September (end Q2).

Astec LifeSciences: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 20% (up from the ~20% earlier guidance); Q1 revenue dip of 8-9% to be recovered in later quarters; CDMO dissilience around 50-52% for the year, with some CDMO shift from H1 to H2.
Astec enterprise margin: Q1 benefited from low-priced raw material and war-driven finished goods price increases; prices now easing, margin normalising. CDMO margins intact.

Oil Palm: FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over the next 4-5 years (LRP); management says it targets double digit; full-year FFB growth guided at high single digit to double digit; margin drop expected to even out over the year.
Animal Nutrition: EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150 per tonne.
Crop Care: no firm FY27 numbers; recovery quantum to be assessed by end-September after cotton herbicide season. Crop Care EBIT margin expected to hold around 26-27% despite tough year.

Dairy: milk procurement prices expected to stay at current elevated levels for 2-3 quarters; packaging inflation expected to ease by August; some impact may persist in Q2; cost initiatives to be doubled down on in H2.
Godrej Foods: live bird trading to decline 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years; branded B2C to be in investment phase for 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Overall business-level capex guidance of roughly INR300-350 crore, phased over 3-4 quarters; includes the integrated palm oil complex (phase 1 started, nursery and CPO mill; seed garden in 18-24 months; refinery later) and specialty fats refinery (rollout late August/early September 2026); management says no new investment beyond this envelope.

Oil Palm area expansion: added about 17,000 hectares last year and on track to repeat this year; LRP target to take area from about 80,000 ha to about 150,000 ha, with Telangana and Northeast expansion; about 50% of plantations are juvenile (0-4 years).
New capex hurdle: IRR of around 16-18% required for new assets; management says the specialty fats downstream business, when scaled, adds roughly 200 bps to overall EBITDA profile.

Godrej Foods: investments in automation of plants and advertising behind branded B2C; NPD pipeline including chicken momos (launched about 4 months ago) and wet momos (planned in 3-4 months), and frozen chicken category push.
demand_pricing: Animal Nutrition: revenue +12.6% on demand and realisations; cattle feed volume +15%, fish feed volume up ~20%+ (about 7% of segment), cattle feed about 55-56% of segment; total segment volume +7% as poultry was deliberately cut in unprofitable geographies. Management says it passed on about 60-70% of commodity (maize) inflation.

Oil Palm: revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations; oil extraction ratio 18.8% vs 18.4%; FFB volume broadly flat against a strong early-monsoon base last year. Segment margin dipped on a pricing-formula change that management calls one-off.

Crop Care: revenue -16.2% on a 40% June rainfall deficit delaying sowing; cotton herbicide volume hit. Ashitaka (maize) and Takai (paddy insecticide) together 18-20% of Q1 sales; July said to be better than last year's base. Management said no share loss to competitors; cited product-mix differences versus peers.

Dairy (CDPL): volume +8% and value +11.5%; value-added share 49% vs 42%. Packaging inflation (linked to crude/LPG after Middle East conflict) and milk procurement prices hurt margin; industry passed on about 70% of price increases.

Godrej Foods: B2C (Yummiez and Real Good) volumes +28% (Yummiez +22%), about 32% of Foods business; overall Foods revenue only about 1-2% growth due to planned live bird decline; B2C value growth about 20%.
Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet): strong double-digit growth in volume, value and PBT under new leadership.
risks_watch: Crop Care recovery depends on the cotton herbicide season and erratic rainfall; management will give a firm view only by end-September.
Dairy margin pressure from elevated milk procurement prices (expected to persist 2-3 quarters) and packaging costs, with some impact likely in Q2.
Oil Palm Q1 margin decline (19% to 17% EBIT) attributed to a pricing formula; watch whether H2 margin recovers as management expects.
Astec: CDMO revenue shifting from H1 into H2, and the 8-9% Q1 dip must be recovered to hit the more-than-20% FY27 target.
Animal Nutrition: poultry volume cuts and maize cost volatility; the segment reported volume growth (+7%) lags cattle feed (+15%).
Godrej Foods reported top line stays near flat (1-2%) while B2C invests; profitability is pressured by input costs and the investment phase.
key_quotes: So I would say, yes, there has been a hit in the quarter 1, which has very clearly come because of this weather pattern.
Nothing crosses our bridge broadly beyond -- until we are doing an IRR of around 16% to 18%, and this meets that bridge for us.
But I think one thing we're still pretty confident of is that we'll be able to target a double -digit growth still.
We have a tight filter on this very clearly. This is a high ROCE business for us.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Oil Palm, Animal Nutrition and Astec, but cautious on Crop Care and the consolidated guidance, which management says will be narrowed only at end-September. Several answers stressed one-off factors (packaging, pricing formula, weather) while deferring specifics on Crop Care and dairy margins.
